web_evidence.title: The Exorcist: The Definitive Edition — publisher sample
web_evidence.note: Penguin's authorized sample supplies the complete prologue and opening of Part I. A nonparticipating narrator externally narrates Merrin and then Chris as he and she while moving into each character's thoughts, establishing third-person narration across two opening sections.

web_evidence.title: BOOK VERSUS FILM: An Epic Study of The Exorcist
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly says the 1971 book follows Chris's third-person viewpoint and that Karras and Kinderman take over when the action shifts; these are changes of focal character within third-person narration, not changes of grammatical person.

person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third person, with focalization moving among Merrin, Chris, Karras, Kinderman, and others. Multiple sustained Goodreads passages independently expose that external position, and Penguin's authorized opening agrees; the whole-book review explicitly identifies the same third-person structure across focal-character shifts. First-person forms in the quote set occur in dialogue, biblical or other paratext, gnomic language, and local thought rather than autonomous base sections. No evidence supports sustained first- or second-person narration or an alternating-person structure. The main limitation is that the authorized excerpt covers only the opening and is from the later definitive edition, but the 1971-derived interior quotes and the review's explicit treatment of the original version resolve that scope issue.
